analysis.title: CIO Weekly: Seeing the Rate Hikes Through the Holds
key_insights: The Fed, ECB and BoJ all held rates last week as expected and are waiting until their December meetings before potentially hiking again. Neuberger says the holds should not be read as pauses yet.

Neuberger expects a broadly synchronized but relatively short tightening cycle across the Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoE to contain inflation. Local macro and political dynamics will set the timing and extent of each move.
The Fed saw two dissents in favor of a quarter-point hike. The elevated PCE print followed hot CPI and PPI data, and the inflation trend extends to the other economies and the U.K.
The BoE meets Thursday and is expected to hike for the first time since August 2023.

Chair Warsh's press conference was moderately dovish and starkly different in tone from September's. He stressed the committee's data-dependent lean and its willingness to accumulate more data, and highlighted the tightening of financial conditions since the September hike.

After the Fed meeting the market modestly reduced pricing of an aggressive hiking cycle. Long-end rates rose and short-end rates fell. Going into the meeting the market had priced a quarterly path of hikes through June 2027.

Neuberger's base case is a 25 bp Fed hike in December followed by a potentially lengthy pause, with the neutral rate settling around 4.00-4.25%. The tail risk is more hikes if energy prices stay elevated or if inflation feeds through to core.
Neuberger expects the BoJ to hike 25 bp in December, with another possibly in Q2 next year. Underlying Japanese inflation has risen steadily this year and has broadly reached the 2% target.

The ECB faces high energy costs, French government bond volatility and a succession race, since Lagarde will step down in February next year. European gas rose above EUR100/MWh for the first time in four years on the threat of a re-escalation in the Iran conflict.

The ECB statement cited stable underlying inflation, wage growth and tightening financial conditions as reasons to hold. It said for the first time that higher energy prices for longer would weigh on growth, giving the statement a broadly dovish tone.
Neuberger thinks an ECB December hike is likely if gas stays above the EUR77 level in the ECB's adverse scenario, and expects a pause next year as focus shifts from inflation to growth.

Neuberger expects US rates to be range-bound around current levels with a bias lower on any risk-off move. It holds a long-duration bias in the US because the market prices more hikes than the Fed has projected.

In Europe Neuberger moved slightly longer, concentrating in the 5-10 year part of the curve. It returned France to neutral, calling the sell-off largely overdone, and sees convergence opportunities in Italy and Greece at 5-7 years and in Central and Eastern Europe.

tension_points.bull_case: The Fed's dovish hold and tighter financial conditions let it wait, so only one 25 bp hike in December followed by a lengthy pause, which supports a long-duration bias.
tension_points.bear_case: Two dissents favored a hike, and elevated PCE, CPI and PPI prints plus high energy prices could feed through to core inflation and force more hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy prices staying elevated or a feed-through to core inflation.
